Strong Regions, Strong EuropeEU Week of Regions and Cities 2026 · Playbook
High-level session · Tuesday 13 October 2026

Making the right
to stay a reality

Opportunities for our communities and our prosperity
Brussels, 13 October 2026 · Graphic recording by Teresa Aledo, Visible Thinking
The question on the table

One in three Europeans are living in declining regions. Young people are most likely to leave, and access to jobs, housing, and, of course, services shape these life-changing decisions.Méabh Mc Mahon, moderator

Expert knowledge

The keynote

Raffaele Fitto, Executive Vice-President for Cohesion and Reforms, European Commission

A simple yet powerful idea

The right to stay is a simple yet powerful idea. Every European should have the opportunity to live and prosper, to build a [future] in the place they call home.

Mobility should be a free choice, not a necessity driven by a lack of job opportunities, a lack of essential services, or a lack of decent living conditions.

Good reasons to stay

These are not luxuries; they are the basic conditions people need to live, work, and build the future in their communities.

The right conditions are specific to each territory. One size does not fit all.

This is a shared effort. The right to stay will only succeed with engagement and ownership at every level.

700+ contributions to the call for evidence27 Member StatesStrategy due early 2027
Roundtable echoes & insights

Five ways to stay

Five territories, five different realities. Each one shows what staying needs in a specific place.

Sparsely populated areasEconomic stagnationDiverse EU territoriesRural border regionOutmigration of the young
Sparsely populated areas

Finland

Anna-Kaisa Ikonen, Minister of Local and Regional Government

Leaving your home [should be] a choice, not a necessity. And one needs to have a right to stay, but also a reason to stay.

Where there is work and opportunities, people stay (…) With vibrancy comes people, and with people comes services.

The right to stay is built locally by businesses and people, and our job is to create the conditions for them to succeed.

Keeping our eastern border areas populated (…) is a crucial and fundamental security issue for us.

Dream big, and then just steam ahead together.

1,300 km border with RussiaKajaani: from paper mill to supercomputer
Economic stagnation

European Parliament

Antonella Sberna, Vice-President

You are best placed to know the specificity of your local communities (…) that is why the solutions proposed have to be based on these real needs.

The fact that you do have the right to stay in your home region can boost the economy and the competitiveness of your region.

We cannot be strong regions without strong and resilient regions and communities.

27,000 people at risk of leaving her province near Rome in 10 years
Diverse EU territories

Committee of the Regions

Vasco Alves Cordeiro, President of the COTER Commission

The right to stay, the freedom to stay, it must be more than words.

For a lot of time, Europe has worked and built freedom of movement, and here comes a time where we are all discussing the freedom to stay.

You don't make people stay by a decree.

Competitiveness does not oppose cohesion, but competitiveness alone cannot achieve what cohesion can achieve.

The right to stay (…) equals a democratic asset.

Rural border region

Extremadura

Pablo Hurtado Pardo, Director-General for EU Affairs and External Action

It's not about convincing people not to leave. It's about ensuring that staying is a real option for them.

Living in a sparsely populated region doesn't mean and shouldn't mean lower opportunities. It should mean true equal opportunities, independently of where you've decided to live.

Small-scale projects are what European construction is all about.

400+ km border with PortugalInterreg POCTEP
Outmigration of the young

Celje, Slovenia

Matija Kovač, Mayor

Create the good opportunities for people to really return and to be able to return to their own environments.

Local environments are responsible for establishing an atmosphere in which people can feel well, they can feel active and involved, they can co-decide.

Where will you live? (…) How will your neighbourhood look, and what can you do as a citizen?

300 public apartments by 2032Magnet project · EUIParticipatory budget
Closing remarks

Behind every statistic

Dubravka Šuica, Commissioner for the Mediterranean

Behind every statistic on depopulation there is a personal story: a young person who cannot find a job, a family that cannot access essential services, a community that gradually loses its future.

A successful region is not only one that attracts investment; it is also one where people see a fair future for themselves and their families.

Migration can help, but it cannot solve the problem.

Demographic change cannot be an afterthought in our investment decisions. It must become part of how we define successful cohesion policy.

The success of European integration should not be measured only by how freely people can move (…) but also how freely they can choose to stay.

Fertility 1.34 vs 2.1 neededOver 65: 1/5 today, 1/3 in 205080% of EU territory is rural
Outcomes

The shifts the panel agreed on.

Mobility is very important from all points of view, but the fact that you do have the right to stay in your home region can boost the economy.Antonella Sberna, European Parliament

People will stay if they don't feel they are abandoned somewhere in remote areas.Vasco Alves Cordeiro, Committee of the Regions

Each municipality, each region has their strengths (…) it's important that we build on these strengths.Anna-Kaisa Ikonen, Finland

This participation has to be done in all kinds of levels.Matija Kovač, Celje

Our investment should not only help regions grow economically. They should also help communities keep their loved ones close by, particularly their young people.Dubravka Šuica

An enormous ability to change our border into an opportunity.Pablo Hurtado Pardo, Extremadura

Next steps

From words to the ground

We will decide this by the end of this year when an agreement is reached about the next MFF.Vasco Alves Cordeiro

  • The Right to Stay strategy, to be presented early next year.
  • National and Regional Partnership Plans, with the right to stay as a specific objective.
  • The 2028–2034 budget, described as the turning point for cohesion.
  • Interreg after 2027, with funding kept for small-scale projects.

High-level session · Wednesday 14 October 2026

A cohesion policy
for a competitive Union

Brussels, 14 October 2026 · Graphic recording by Teresa Aledo, Visible Thinking
The question on the table

Can Europe become more competitive without leaving some of its regions behind?

Where in Europe will that growth happen, and who will actually feel it?Johannes Tralla, moderator

Many of our capital regions (…) are racing ahead, but they don't automatically pull the rest of the country with them, do they?Johannes Tralla, moderator

Expert knowledge

The keynote

Raffaele Fitto, Executive Vice-President for Cohesion and Reforms, European Commission

Many engines, not a few

Europe's economy is not powered by just a few engines, but by [many].

Strong regions, strong Europe. Europe can only be as strong as its regions, and European competitiveness cannot be achieved by a few regions acting alone. It must be built across Europe in every region.

The benefits and opportunities of technology must be felt everywhere.

Competitiveness has a place

Businesses are more likely to invest where they can find the skills they need, reliable infrastructure and good connections, and people are more likely to (…) build their future where they can find good jobs, affordable housing, and quality of public services.

There is no single model of competitiveness.

Turn Europe's regional diversity into a source of competitive advantage.

Demand from the ground

Competitiveness is a concrete demand coming directly from the ground, from our regions, local authorities, and communities.

58% of cohesion investment, around €220 bn, supports competitiveness€35 bn reallocated at mid-term review€15 bn+ to competitiveness

Your voices matter

You know the strengths of your regions. You know where investments are needed, where opportunities exist, and where barriers remain.

The success of the next investments will depend not only on the resources available, but on how well we use them, and how well we connect European priorities with the realities on the ground.

Roundtable echoes & insights

Five realities, one Europe

A smaller Member State, a long border, an island, an industrial engine and the private sector.

Smaller Member State

Slovenia

Monika Kirbiš Rojas, Minister for Local Self-Government, Cohesion and Regional Development

Intervention delivered in Slovenian. Literal quotes to be added from the interpretation channel.

Border with Russia and Belarus

Lithuania

Rūta Carik, Vice-Minister of Finance

It's the most difficult moment for a mother not to know if their children are safe.

Security and competitiveness, they're inseparable. They grow together.

It's like a snake eating its own tail. Weaker investment means fewer opportunities.

We do not choose this as our destiny (…) but we cannot do it alone.

Island

Corsica

Marie-Antoinette Maupertuis, President of the Assembly of Corsica

Intervention delivered in French. Key ideas, paraphrased: every region has its own competitive advantage; reform and investment are not opposites; regions ask for opportunities and connectivity, not compensation; Europe needs foresight to face the next shocks.

Industrialised

Lombardy

Raffaele Cattaneo, Undersecretary to the Presidency, International and EU Relations

Cohesion and [competitiveness] are the two faces of the same [medal].

Please don't confuse cohesion policies with a charity (…) like an economic ambulance.

[Regions should have a central role], not just as beneficiaries, but as a policymaker, as a planner of the cohesion policies.

In Italy, we know the word "[concorrenza]" from the Latin: run together.

Private sector

BusinessEurope

Lúcio Vinhas de Souza, Chief Economist

You must strike a balance between both flexibility and predictability.

Cohesion is not a crisis adjustment mechanism. It's a long-term structural policy.

When you bring the private sector in, the outcomes of cohesion funds increase significantly.

Outcomes

What has to change

The shifts the panel agreed on.

Cohesion versus competitiveness→Two faces of the same medal

European Union competitiveness reflects the competitiveness of our member states, our regions, our cities, and our companies.Lúcio Vinhas de Souza, BusinessEurope

Charity and compensation→Investment in the conditions to compete

It's not charity; it's investment. We invest that money, and we should benefit from it.Rūta Carik, Lithuania

Top-down→Bottom-up, from the territories

We cannot invest everywhere in exactly the same way and expect same results.Rūta Carik, Lithuania

Fixing weaknesses→Unlocking strengths

Strong regions are not only about addressing weaknesses; they're about unlocking their strengths.Rūta Carik, Lithuania

Security as a side issue→Security as a condition for growth

Businesses invest and families build their future where they see opportunity and predictability.Rūta Carik, Lithuania

Simplification by centralising→Simplification that trusts regions

Simplification cannot [mean] centralization.Raffaele Cattaneo, Lombardy

Next steps

What stays open

Who decides where the money goes?

Well, that perhaps is not exactly settled.Johannes Tralla, moderator

  • How regions take part in drafting the National and Regional Partnership Plans.
  • How the 2028–2034 budget balances flexibility with predictability.
  • How to simplify rules without centralising decisions.
